Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Depressive symptom scores (CES-D) did not differ between T2DM patients with vitamin D insufficiency and those with normal vitamin D.
Sentence: "There was no significant difference between groups with regard to the indices of blood lipid, liver function, and scores in CES-D and PSQI."
Measured as: CES-D score
Population: 132 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Intervention: Vitamin D insufficiency (plasma 25(OH)D <29 ng/mL), measured not given
Comparator: Normal vitamin D (25(OH)D ≥29 ng/mL)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 132
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum magnesium levels were associated with lower depression severity (HAM-D) in both groups.
Sentence: "In both groups, magnesium levels decreased as the severity of depression (measured by the HAM-D scale) increased."
Measured as: depression severity (HAM-D)
Population: Patients with major depressive disorder attending psychiatry outpatient department, with and without suicidal behavior
Intervention: Serum magnesium level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Not applicable (association across participants)
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 200
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
